decision.title: The timezone database (packet )
decision.summary: The optional feature "timezone-database" reads one TZif file per zone from the host's resolver at first use, serving fn:civil-timezone and the formatting functions' $place, with tzdata vendored for tests.

body.p: , after , , , , , , . Replaces 's "no tz database" and the FODT0004 place of in fn:civil-timezone.

item.p: Data from the host, TZif: the optional feature sxml_timezone_database_feature() ("timezone-database", src/timezone.c, src/timezone_internal.h) reads zones as the host has them: one TZif file per zone (RFC 8536, versions 1 to 4), asked of the resolver as the new SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_TIMEZONE_DATA (additive in processor.h) under urn:sxml:timezone-data: + a zoneinfo path (a zone name, or zone1970.tab, else zone.tab, for country codes). No compact form and no generator: TZif is the standard format, every Unix host has it in /usr/share/zoneinfo, and one reader serves both hosts and the vendored data. sxml checks a name before it asks (ASCII letters, digits, _ - +, parts between single /), so a resolver can map the path onto a directory. A zone is read at its first use and kept in the processor's feature state; a zone that is not delivered is asked again next time (no negative cache, so a query cannot grow the state with names that do not exist).

Vendored: tzdata 2026e under third_party/tzdata (): the sources, and zoneinfo/ compiled by zic -b slim with the zone tables, 599 files, 237 KB; tools/update-tzdata.sh moves it. The QT4 driver serves it (../tzdata/zoneinfo/ from the catalog), the unit tests read it from the source tree; the sxml command serves the host's /usr/share/zoneinfo; JavaScript hosts answer the kind 'timezone-data'. Nothing is compiled into sxml.

Lookup (RFC 8536, 3.2): type 0 before the first transition, the last transition's type, the footer's TZ string (POSIX XBD 8.3 with RFC 8536's 167-hour and negative times) from the last transition on. Leap second records are skipped (xs:dateTime has no leap seconds). Years beyond ±10^9 get no answer.

fn:civil-timezone (F&O 4.0, 9.7.4): no place is the implicit timezone, the UTC names stay PT0S without the database; any other place is a zone name, looked up at $value's instant ($value without a timezone takes the implicit timezone); FODT0004 without the feature, for an unknown zone, or a year out of range. A country code is not a zone here (the rules say "IANA timezone name").

$place of the formatting functions (9.9.4.8): a zone name adjusts a value with a timezone to the zone's offset at its instant and gives [ZN] its abbreviation; a time alone takes the zone's standard time ("only possible where the value includes a date"). A country code (two ASCII letters, any case) does not adjust; [ZN] names the first zone of the country, in zone1970.tab's order, with the value's offset at that instant (2018-07-01 at -05:00 in "us" is America/Chicago's CDT). An abbreviation that does not start with a letter ("-03") is no name, and an offset with seconds (local mean time) is no xs:dateTime timezone: the fallback format 01:01 is kept, as for an unknown place and no place (format-time-030).

Numbers (release drivers, against 97aedba): fn-civil-timezone 4 to 9 of 9 (XP40 and XQ40); with the dependency olson-timezone turned on, fn-format-dateTime XQ40 83 to 93 of 94 run (not run 9 to 1), XP40 80 to 88 (not run 14 to 6): all 8 olson-timezone cases and 025c/025e; fn-format-time XQ40 96 to 97 (025c); app-spec-examples XQ40 1,479 to 1,480 and XP40 1,346 to 1,347 (fo-test-fn-civil-timezone-003); fn-format-date and misc-BuiltInKeywords unchanged; XT40 format-date and format-date-en unchanged. The packet's gate (all 14 cases) is met.

Size (wasm preset): sxml-full.wasm 3,564,851 to 3,575,555 bytes (+10,704; gzipped 1,085,933 to 1,090,270), within its 4,000,000 budget; sxml.wasm 2,294,067 to 2,295,933 (+1,866: the two places and the value adjustment, which ask for the feature), already over its 2,200,000 budget before (); the CLI module 6,510,188 to 6,521,732. No budget changes.
Not done: the dynamic context has no default place (a host setting would be an additive header change); without one, no place keeps the implicit timezone and [ZN] the fallback format.
